hints: Focus on oxidation in organic chemistry as gaining oxygen or losing hydrogen, so track how the functional group changes.
Notice that $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde, and Tollens reagent is a mild oxidising agent that converts aldehydes to carboxylic acids.
Compare the other reagents to see if they reduce, dehydrate or hydrolyse, then pick the one change that adds oxygen to carbon.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for oxidation**

In organic chemistry, oxidation means gaining O or losing H. Reduction is the opposite, losing O or gaining H.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{oxidation = gain of O / loss of H}$$

**Identify what Tollens does to an aldehyde**

Tollens reagent, $\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+$, is a mild oxidising agent. It oxidises an aldehyde to a carboxylate ion (the alkaline form of a carboxylic acid) while silver(I) is reduced to silver mirror.

Reaction type:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$$
Here carbon gains an oxygen, so this is oxidation.

**Check why the others are not oxidation**

With $\text{LiAlH}_4$, the aldehyde gains hydrogen to form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so that is reduction. With concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, the alcohol loses water to form an alkene, which is dehydration (elimination). With dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the ester $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ is split by water into acid plus alcohol, which is hydrolysis. None of these is a gain of O by the carbon skeleton.

**Conclude the answer**

Only the aldehyde plus Tollens reagent shows a clear oxidation of the organic molecule. That matches the oxidation reaction.

options.A: Correct. Tollens reagent oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids (as carboxylate salts in alkali). The $\text{-CHO}$ group gains oxygen to become $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$, so the organic compound is oxidised and a silver mirror forms.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a strong reducing agent, not an oxidising agent. It donates hydride to the aldehyde to give the primary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so the organic is reduced by gaining hydrogen.
options.C: Incorrect. Concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ with a primary alcohol causes acid-catalysed dehydration (elimination) to an alkene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Water is lost but there is no net gain of oxygen, so this is not oxidation.
options.D: Incorrect. Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ with the ester $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ causes acid hydrolysis to ethanoic acid plus ethanol. Bonds are broken by water with no change in oxidation level, so this is hydrolysis, not oxidation.
